title: Modular private-deployment pricing matrix and RFQ response framework
creator: Sofia Moreno
description: Create a modular pricing matrix and accompanying RFQ/SEC questionnaire response framework for Private/VPC and on-prem deployments. Goal: enable sales and solutions engineering to quickly assemble compliant proposals (license fee, support tier, and upgrade cadence) tailored to enterprise procurement and security teams. This ticket scopes the experiment design, canonical pricing table, configurable support tier definitions, upgrade cadence options, and a templated set of responses for common security questionnaire items.
background: Enterprise prospects repeatedly request variable license terms (flat seat/instance license, commit credits, and overage pricing), multiple support tiers, and clear upgrade/maintenance schedules for on-prem or VPC installs. Current collateral is fragmented: sales playbooks, engineering runbooks, and ad-hoc legal responses. This initiative consolidates a modular bundle approach so proposals are faster and consistent while minimizing legal/security review churn.
goals: 1) Produce a canonical pricing matrix with combinable building blocks (base license, capacity credits, optional HA add-on, and patch/upgrade SLA tiers). 2) Define 3 support tiers with SLO examples, on-call windows, and response/patch cadence. 3) Produce a 1-page RFQ response template and a security-questionnaire FAQ that covers top 30 enterprise items. 4) Validate with two pilot deals and iterate.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pricing matrix documented as a single spreadsheet and referenced in the sales playbook.
- Support tier definitions and example contracts/procurement language written.
- RFQ template and security questionnaire FAQ drafted and reviewed by Legal and Security.
- Two pilot deals used the framework and feedback tracked in follow-ups.
- Security review sign-off obtained (security_review_required=true).
work_items: Inventory existing contract language and past RFQ answers (Sales, Legal, Security)
Draft modular pricing building blocks: base license, per-GPU credit banding, reserved capacity discounts, upgrade/maintenance add-ons
Define support tiers: Core (business hours), Priority (24x5), Platinum (24x7) with example SLAs and escalation paths
Design upgrade cadence options: managed rolling updates, scheduled customer-controlled upgrades, certified minor/major timelines
Create RFQ template and security-questionnaire FAQ (top-30) for common auditor questions
Pilot with Solutions Eng on 2 deals and collect structured feedback
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Too many combinable options creates quoting complexity. Mitigation: restrict to a 3x3 matrix of primary choices and preset bundles for common segments.

Risk: Security answers require engineering time to validate. Mitigation: create a triage matrix that flags items needing engineering sign-off and maintain a live 'engineering answers' doc with owners.
Risk: Legal negotiation on upgrade commitments may increase liability. Mitigation: provide optional upgrade SLAs (pay-for-priority) and standardized warranty language vetted by Legal.
Risk: Pricing conflicts with Dedicated capacity commitments. Mitigation: include mapping guidance that translates pricing building blocks to Dedicated/Hosted equivalence for sales conversations.
